exact_all_length_result.assumptions: Integer d>=2, strictly positive diagonal P=diag(p_i), sum_i p_i=1. The frozen task requires rational p_i; both finite-dimensional proofs also justify positive real p_i. For every k>=2 use rho_P=|0><0|/2 direct-sum P/2, sigma_P=rho_P^tensor k, d prepend colors, the retained two-seed root, and the same charge-pinched bulk G1 on sufficiently deep initial words. F=(C^d)^tensor k, H_zeta=Tr_F[(I tensor zeta)G1]+2Q-kI. Minimize Tr(sigma_P H_zeta^2) over every density zeta on F, including complex coherent and entangled states.
exact_all_length_result.formula: Let s=1-Tr(P^2). The unique t>0 solves sum_i(1-t/p_i)_+=1; put z_i=(1-t/p_i)_+, Z=diag(z_i), B=Tr[P(I-Z)^2]. Then v_k(P)=s k(k-1)/4+(B-s)C_k/2 and zeta_*=sum_i z_i (|i><i|)^tensor k attains it. C_k=sum_(n=0)^(k-2)(k-1-n)Pr(S_n=0), for a fair walk; odd returns vanish and Pr(S_2n=0)=binom(2n,n)/4^n. With N=floor((k-2)/2), C_k=(2N+1)binom(2N,N)4^-N[k-1-2N/3]. Thus v_k(P)/k^2 ->s/4.
exact_all_length_result.active_set: For J={i:p_i>t}, t=(|J|-1)/(sum_(i in J)1/p_i), B=sum_(i not in J)p_i+(|J|-1)t, and |J|>=2. Threshold ties p_i=t have z_i=0. Rational P gives exact rational t,z,B,v. The optimizer is correlated separable and analytic; it is not a physical bath initializer.
exact_all_length_result.all_competitor_argument: The algebraic word cancellation remains valid on superpositions. Conditional color weight P^tensor q is invariant under input permutations. Input/input sectors cost 2s; critical input/bath sectors cost f(R)=Tr[P(I-R)^2]=sum_i p_i(1-R_ii)^2+sum_(i<j)(p_i+p_j)|R_ij|^2. Pinching lowers this strictly convex simplex problem, giving the threshold minimizer. Other export sectors are merely nonnegative for arbitrary competitors; each repeated pure prefix cancels them before mixing. One zeta_* therefore attains all lower bounds simultaneously. Fair charge probabilities remain 2^-k and give the unchanged collision sum; no finite matrix extrapolation proves the result.

correct_dual_and_support.certificate: T_k(X)=Tr_A[(X tensor I)G1]. At the optimum only, H_* commutes with sigma_P. Let Delta=diag((t-p_i)_+). Both reports obtain D_k=T_k(sigma_P H_*)=v_k I+sum_(m=0)^(k-2) w_(k,m) Delta^(m)>=v_k I, with every w_(k,m)>0 and sum_m w_(k,m)=C_k/2. The weights are one half the fair-walk probabilities of prefix deficit m and prefix height equal to independent middle deficit, summed over prefix+middle length <=k-2.
correct_dual_and_support.support_and_equality: With W=span{|i>:p_i>=t}, ker(D_k-v_k I)=W^tensor(k-1) tensor C^d. The optimizer is supported there; support alone is insufficient. For every density zeta, Tr(sigma_P H_zeta^2)=v_k+2Tr[zeta(D_k-v_k I)]+Tr[sigma_P(H_zeta-H_*)^2]. Strict positivity gives optimality exactly when H_zeta=H_*; its representing density need not be unique. The general gradient is T_k((sigma_P H+H sigma_P)/2), not T_k(sigma_P H) for an arbitrary noncommuting competitor.
correct_dual_and_support.failed_scalar_transfer: The old scalar dual holds exactly when min_i p_i>=t. Strictly excluded p_i<t create slack, but rank deficiency alone does not. At P=(2/5,2/5,1/5), t=1/5 and Z=diag(1/2,1/2,0), B=2/5, yet Delta=0 and the dual is scalar. This boundary correction must accompany any support-transition summary.
